# Brian on Things

> Practical guides to Python, Rust and backend systems by software engineer Brian Obot, plus deep dives into low-level internals, physics and maths.

This is the personal blog of Brian Obot, a software engineer and Python & Rust developer. It has in-depth, practical articles on Python (FastAPI, Django, Pydantic, performance), Rust (ownership, lifetimes, modules, bytes), low-level systems and developer tooling, written from hands-on experience.

## About

- [About Brian Obot: Software Engineer, Python & Rust Developer](https://brianobot.tech/about/): I'm Brian Obot, a software engineer and freelance Python & Rust developer building backend systems, contributing to open source and writing about software.
- [Hire a Freelance Python & Rust Developer – Brian Obot](https://brianobot.tech/hire/): Freelance Python and Rust developer for backend APIs, FastAPI and Django services, Rust web services and performance work. Open to contracts and open source.
- [Projects](https://brianobot.tech/projects/): Open source work by Brian Obot: FastAPI and Django project templates, Rust CLI tools for load testing and API security, plus learning repos from Rust to C.

## Posts

- [Introduction to Bytes in Rust. Part 1](https://brianobot.tech/blog/working-with-bytes-in-rust/): A beginner-friendly introduction to bytes in Rust: bits, bytes and hexadecimal, why computers use binary, and how Rust represents byte collections and strings.
- [What I Learned (and Wish I'd Done Differently) at TechCabal's Moonshot](https://brianobot.tech/blog/what-i-learned-at-techcabals-moonshot-2026/): Lessons from my first TechCabal Moonshot after moving to Lagos: the sessions, the exhibition floor, the people, and three things I'd do differently next time.
- [Learning Technical Skills in the Age of SI](https://brianobot.tech/blog/learning-technical-skills-in-the-age-of-si/): Why learn technical skills when AI writes code faster? My case for mastery in the age of super intelligence, and what chess teaches us about deep understanding.
- [Common Gotchas When Working with Rust as a Python Developer](https://brianobot.tech/blog/common-gotchas-when-working-with-rust-as-a-python-developer/): Six gotchas Python developers hit when moving to Rust: flushing stdout, ownership and borrowing, Result-based errors, concurrency, unsafe code and performance.
- [Stop Writing Manual Validation: Master Pydantic](https://brianobot.tech/blog/stop-writing-manual-validation-master-pydantic/): Replace manual validation in Python with Pydantic: models, type annotations, data coercion, custom validators, serialization and using Pydantic with FastAPI.
- [I Finally Understand References and Lifetimes in Rust](https://brianobot.tech/blog/i-finally-understand-references-and-lifetimes-in-rust/): References and lifetimes in Rust explained: how borrowing and ownership work, what lifetime annotations mean, and how lifetime elision keeps code clean.
- [Mastering Python Performance: The Small Tweaks That Make Big Speed](https://brianobot.tech/blog/mastering-python-performance-small-tweaks-big-speed/): Practical ways to speed up Python: sets for lookups, built-ins, lru_cache and concurrency, plus how memory management, the GIL and Big O affect performance.
- [Mastering the Crate and Module System in Rust](https://brianobot.tech/blog/mastering-the-crate-and-module-system-in-rust/): A guide to Rust's crate and module system: packages vs crates, modules, paths and visibility, dependency management and how to organise large Rust codebases.
- [Setting Up Rust Analyzer to work for Non-Cargo-Based Rust Projects](https://brianobot.tech/blog/setting-up-rust-analyzer-for-non-cargo-rust-projects/): Get Rust Analyzer autocomplete, type hints and go-to-definition in single-file Rust programs without Cargo, using rust-project.json. Handy for Advent of Code.
- [Starting Today, I'm Going Deeper into Game Development with Rust](https://brianobot.tech/blog/starting-today-im-choosing-to-go-deeper/): The start of my game development series in Rust: why I'm exploring game engines and storytelling, why I chose Rust and the Bevy engine, and the road ahead.
- [How to Implement Autocomplete Functionality for Your CLI Program in Python](https://brianobot.tech/blog/autocomplete-for-your-cli-program-in-python/): Add tab autocompletion to a Python CLI with the built-in readline module: build a vocabulary-based completer, bind the Tab key and use it in a command loop.
- [How to generate an ERD for your Database with Python in seconds](https://brianobot.tech/blog/generate-an-erd-for-your-database-with-python/): Generate an entity-relationship diagram (ERD) of your database in seconds with Python and eralchemy2, plus fixes for common Graphviz install issues on macOS.
- [Zed: The Text Editor Reimagined for the Modern Developer](https://brianobot.tech/blog/zed-the-text-editor-reimagined-for-the-modern-developer/): A guide to setting up the Zed editor: why it's worth trying, how it compares with VS Code, installing the Zed CLI, choosing a theme and learning key bindings.
- [6 Python Tips That Quietly Level Up Your Code](https://brianobot.tech/blog/some-python-tips-that-quietly-level-up-your-code/): Six small Python tips for cleaner code: inline blocks, underscores in numbers, dict comprehensions, setdefault, contextlib.suppress and one-line statements.
- [My FastAPI Project Blueprint](https://brianobot.tech/blog/my-favorite-fastapi-project-blueprint/): The FastAPI project structure I use on every new project: how I lay out routers, schemas, settings, dependencies and middleware so large codebases stay sane.
- [How I Hacked FastAPI BackgroundTasks for Real-Time Progress Updates (Without Celery)](https://brianobot.tech/blog/how-i-hacked-fastapi-backgroundtasks-for-real-time-progress-updates/): How I used FastAPI BackgroundTasks to run long AI jobs in the background and report real-time progress through a status endpoint, without reaching for Celery.
